elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New 12(c): "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Client and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12(c) covers "all third-party claims, actions, expenses, losses and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees" in favour of "Client and its affiliates".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(i): "any allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any related software or deliverable infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right" — tracks the actual defined service/deliverable set in this agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(ii): "any breach by TrueLink of applicable law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or other data of or provided by Client caused by TrueLink" — causation tied to Vendor and covering all Customer data categories.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party written notice of any claim for which indemnity is sought".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 12(a) as amended is limited to "(i) the Client Content, and (ii) any violation by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the former breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product-injury limbs are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: 12(c)(i) provides a third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in Client's favour.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification-based exclusion is required and none is needed since the drafted indemnity is unqualified in Customer's favour.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; absence of a combination carve-out does not defeat it (the omission is Customer-favourable).

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification carve-out is required.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The rendered text contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation anywhere in Section 12; to reach the fallback the drafter would need an express clause requiring TrueLink to procure the right to continue use, modify or replace the infringing Interface/Services.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears in the rendered language; a clause refunding applicable fees where the alternative remedies are not commercially reasonable would be required.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability super-cap of 3x annual fees is stated in or cross-referenced from the inserted 12(c).

reasons: Preferred level is complete: new Section 12(c) supplies the express defend/indemnify duty for Client and affiliates, all four covered claim categories (IP infringement, breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and the full notice / defence-control / reasonable-cooperation procedure; amended 12(a) narrows Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's violation of law.

Fallback level is incomplete (procure/modify/replace, refund and 3x super-cap all absent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is satisfied; the comment correctly offers the fallback as a negotiating position rather than relying on it.

Minimal: the only deletions are the Client-indemnity limbs (breach of Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site, product injury) that the Customer-indemnity-narrowing element requires, and the favourable existing 12(b) TrueLink breach indemnity is retained. The insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or unrelated boilerplate.

Preserves intent: 12(c) is drafted in the same style and defined terms as the existing clause (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client Content, Credit Data), leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict retained 12(b) — the overlap with the general breach indemnity is additive rather than inconsistent.

Finding status 'deviation' is correct: the original Section 12 contained no Vendor IP infringement indemnity at all and no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, which fails the fallback on a material term.
